casey:go-vegetarian:
Your current carbon footprint sits at 10,510 kg CO2e per year, and going fully vegetarian would cut that by 2,605 kg CO2e — a 25% reduction from a single dietary shift. That's the equivalent of 43 trees growing for ten years, which is a meaningful impact without touching your car, home heating, or travel habits.

Start by identifying the 5 red meat meals you currently eat each week and find one direct plant-based substitute for each — lentil bolognese instead of beef, chickpea curry instead of lamb, and so on. Since the recommendation keeps your dairy at its current medium level, you don't need to overhaul everything at once; just focus on replacing the meat portion of each meal. Spend one week cooking through your substitute list and note which two or three you'd actually eat again — build your routine around those rather than trying to master a wide variety immediately. Once those meals feel normal, stock your freezer with batch-cooked portions so that busy nights don't push you back to old habits.
casey:next-car-ev:
Your estimated footprint is 10,510 kg CO2e per year, and switching your current gas car to an electric vehicle is the single most impactful change you can make. Based on your existing 320 km a week of driving, an EV charged on Ontario's grid would save 2,516 kg CO2e per year — that's 24% of your total footprint, equivalent to 42 trees growing for ten years. Ontario's grid is relatively clean, which means an EV here delivers real, meaningful savings compared to many other provinces.

Start by researching EV models that fit your weekly driving routine, since 320 km a week is well within the range most modern EVs handle comfortably. Look into federal and provincial incentives available in Ontario to reduce the upfront cost, and identify whether home charging (a Level 2 outlet) is feasible for your living situation. When your current vehicle is due for replacement — or sooner if it makes financial sense — make the EV your default choice rather than another gas vehicle.
casey:swap-beef-plant:
Your current carbon footprint is estimated at 10,510 kg CO2e per year, and one of the clearest opportunities sits on your plate. Because you're currently eating 5 red meat meals a week, shifting just 2 of those to beans, lentils, or tofu would save 998 kg CO2e per year — that's 9% of your total footprint, equivalent to 17 trees growing for ten years.

Start by picking two specific days in your weekly routine — say Tuesday and Thursday — and commit to those as your plant-protein days. Stock your kitchen with a few easy staples: canned lentils, chickpeas, or firm tofu, which take no more time to prepare than ground beef. If you find a couple of go-to recipes in the first two weeks, the habit becomes automatic rather than effortful. Track the change simply: after a month, check whether those 2 meals have held, then decide if you want to go further. This single swap, sustained across 52 weeks, is the entire ask — no other changes required to claim that 998 kg reduction.
sam:one-fewer-long-haul:
Your current footprint sits at 5,631 kg CO2e per year, and given that you have no car and eat vegetarian, your 6 long-haul return flights are doing the heaviest lifting in that total. Dropping just one of those trips would save 759 kg CO2e per year — that's 13% of your entire footprint removed with a single decision.

Start by looking at your flight calendar now and identifying which trip is the most optional — a leisure trip you could replace with a local Ontario destination, or a visit you could combine with another trip in the same year. If the trip is for staying connected with people you care about, explore whether a visit every other year rather than annually would still feel meaningful. You might also check whether any of your 6 trips could be consolidated — for example, combining two shorter visits into one longer stay reduces the number of return flights without necessarily reducing the time spent.

The equivalent of 13 trees growing for ten years is a real, tangible result from one calendar adjustment. Decide on the trip to drop before your next booking window opens, so the choice is made before momentum takes over.
